target: banner petal (PO_0025324); the blade (limb) is the part of the banner distal to the claw: region 'distal' of the banner petal until a petal-limb class exists
reason: Narrower than the banner petal: floras measure the blade apart from the claw ('recurved at about 40° from claw'). PO has no petal lamina or claw class, and corolla limb (FLOPO_0986012) is for fused corollas. Grounding it to the whole banner would mix blade lengths with whole-petal lengths. If blade/claw pairs recur across floras, propose a 'petal limb' class.
A dimension, not a part: the length of the frond (vascular leaf, PO_0009025, which has 'frond' as a synonym). Here it is the comparand of a ratio (pattern 10: 'stipe 2/3-3/4 the frond length').
Narrower: the seed proper, without its wing (seed wing FLOPO_0986091) or other appendage. The lengths and colours stated are those of the seed.
Fragment: the container of a count (pattern 03/14), not a structure. Treated like 'per flower' and 'per node' in the previous review.
Fragment: the container of a count (sori per pinnule; pinnule is leaflet PO_0020049). Treated like 'per pinna' in the previous review.

Narrower: a bract placed on, or subtending, a branch. Without context it is unclear whether the branch is an inflorescence branch or a vegetative one, so the general bract class is used rather than inflorescence bract (PO_0009054). 'Subtending' is not parthood, so no container is given.
Ambiguous: 'flank' means the side of whatever is being described (a lip, glume, keel, fruit or ridge). The values given (violet, inflexed, ascending) fit several of these.

target: leaf rachis (PO_0020055) as container; the part is the stretch of rachis between two successive leaflet pairs
reason: A region of the leaf rachis, one in a series of segments between leaflet insertions. Its length is not the rachis length, so do not ground it to the rachis itself. Only one flora uses it, which is not enough for a new class. Keep it with the rachis as container until other floras also need a 'rachis segment'.

target: bract apex (PO_0025154) with container involucral bract (PO_0009045)
reason: An apex region of an existing class. Pattern 12, part with a fixed whole.
Fragment: the container of a count (pattern 03/14).
Exact: 'floret' is a PO synonym of flower ('Asteraceae floret'), and the counts given are those of the pistillate florets of a capitulum.
The apex region of an existing FLOPO anatomy class.
Narrower: the dorsal sporophylls of the dimorphic strobili of Selaginella. 'Dorsal' is not one of the nine positions of pattern 18, so the position is lost until a reviewed position word is added.
Exact: 'funiculus' is already a PO synonym of funicle. The failure to ground is a matcher miss, probably the plural or lemma form.
Exact in sense: a hair ending in a secretory head.
The apex region of an existing FLOPO class. The more general floral spur is used rather than petal spur (PO_0025511), because the spur may belong to a sepal or a labellum.

The sinus between calyx lobes is a phyllome sinus that is part of the calyx, a part with a fixed whole. Some extracted statements are misreadings, such as the Rubiaceae colleters 'coléter globoso' that sit in the sinus.

target: bract margin (PO_0025011) with container inflorescence bract (PO_0009054)
reason: The margin region of an existing class.

Narrower: a misspelling of microphyll, the single-veined leaf of lycophytes ('micrófilo lateral', Selaginella). PO's vascular leaf covers lycophyte leaves; macrophyll and megaphyll are already its synonyms.

target: leaflet (PO_0020049), counted in pairs (count factor 2), as for 'jugate' in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv
reason: A jugum is a pair of opposite leaflets, not a structure of its own. 'Number of juga up to 10' is a count of leaflets in pairs, the existing 'jugate' rule of pattern 03.
Pattern 12: the sex is a quality of the flower, not of the sepal.
Exact in sense: a free carpel-derived fruitlet of an apocarpous fruit, such as Kadsura or Schisandra ('apocarps red to purple'). Annonaceae floras call the same thing a monocarp.

reason: A gland at a position on an existing region; a part with a fixed whole.

target: filament (PO_0009067) with container stamen (PO_0009029); position 'posterior' held
reason: The filament of the posterior (adaxial) stamens of a didynamous androecium. The part is grounded; 'posterior' is not one of the nine positions of pattern 18, so the position needs a reviewed position word.

Narrower: the lemma without its awn (lemma awn, PO_0006032) and callus (floret callus, FLOPO_0986120), both of which have classes of their own. Shape and indumentum statements are about the lemma itself.
Pattern 12: 'male' is a quality of the flower, not of the sepal.
A unit of area density, not a structure. Rates are held by pattern 14.

Ambiguous: it is either the sheath of a cauline leaf on a culm (leaf sheath, PO_0020104) or a sheathing bract or scale leaf on a scape ('scapi vaginis', which would be scale leaf PO_0006003). The two are different classes, and the word alone does not decide between them.
